excerpts.text: John Jumper: UChicago Department of Chemistry alum and the 2024 Nobel Prize winner in Chemistry

John Jumper (PhD ’17) has been awarded the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.](https://news.uchicago.edu/story/uchicago-alum-john-jumper-shares-nobel-prize-model-predicting-protein-structures)**

The **[Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences](https://www.kva.se/en/)** honored Jumper, who received his master’s degree in 2012 and his Ph.D. from the University of Chicago in 2017, along with **[Demis Hassabis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demis_Hassabis),** for their work on "protein structure prediction." The prize is also shared with **[Prof. David Baker](https://www.ipd.uw.edu/david-baker/)** of the University of Washington **["for computational protein design."](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/2024/press-release/#:~:text=The%20Nobel%20Prize%20in%20Chemistry%202024%20is%20about%20proteins%2C%20life's,%3A%20predicting%20proteins'%20complex%20structures.)**
The announcement of the Jumper’s 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry has been met with widespread acclaim.
o **[Nobel Prize in Chemistry Goes to 3 Scientists for Predicting and Creating Proteins | The New York Times](https://www.nytimes.com/2024/10/09/science/nobel-prize-chemistry.html)**
